GF2P8AFFINEINVQB                                             Perform a Galois Inverse Affine
VGF2P8AFFINEINVQB                                                           Transformation
Perform a Galois inverse affine transformation on 64-bit qword blocks of byte data.
Each bit (bit_n) in each byte (byte_n) in each result 64-bit block is a function of the two
corresponding 64-bit source blocks in source operands 1 and 2 (src1blk, src2blk) and the immediate
byte (imm8):
 result.byte[byte_n].bit[bit_n] = odd_parity(src2blk.byte[7-bit_n] & inverse(src1blk.byte[byte_n])) ^
imm8.bit[bit_n]

The odd_parity() function is defined as 1 if the input byte has an odd number of 1 bits in it, and 0
otherwise.
The inverse() function takes a byte as input and returns the byte from the following hexadecimal table
as output:

XMM Encoding
The first source operand is an XMM register. The second source operand is an XMM register, a 128-
bit memory location, or (for EVEX encodings) a broadcast 64-bit memory location. The destination is
a third XMM register. Bits above bit 127 of the YMM/ZMM register that corresponds to the
destination are cleared.
YMM Encoding
The first source operand is a YMM register. The second source operand is a YMM register, a 256-bit
memory location, or (for EVEX encodings) a broadcast 64-bit memory location. The destination is a
third YMM register. Bits above bit 255 of the ZMM register that corresponds to the destination are
cleared.
ZMM Encoding
The first source operand is a ZMM register. The second source operand is a ZMM register, a 512-bit
memory location, or (for EVEX encodings) a broadcast 64-bit memory location. The destination is a
third ZMM register.
The EVEX encoded versions of this instruction write to the destination based on the supplied k mask
per 8-bit element and do not support memory fault suppression.
